review.decision_difference: Choose A because it makes feasibility verification part of the gate itself: continue into the packaged slice only when every essential dependency is available or has a bounded acquisition path; otherwise stop without diverting scarce effort. B chooses the same milestone but exposes the project to premature integration work before resolving those prerequisites.
review.rationale: Both missions identify the same project-specific integration mechanism: proving that Gahyeon's independently validated speech, animation, concurrency, cancellation, and recovery behavior survives a packaged Unreal runtime. Both clearly sequence the vertical slice ahead of migration and identity work. A is stronger because it begins with a bounded prerequisite-and-scope probe, honors the prohibition against assuming Unreal, device, provider, or asset access, and supplies explicit stop conditions before costly integration. B is readily testable but its immediate packaging probe presumes resources that the case says must not be assumed, and its five-turn probe does not fully align with its twenty-interaction completion signal.
